result.rationale: The server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is `z.object({bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email())})` with no uniqueness refine — that exists only in the dialog's client-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema. The handler's uniqueGuests filter only checks `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and the blacklist — it never deduplicates within the request — and then createMany inserts guestsFullDetails as-is. So a direct mutation with duplicate emails in the array would create duplicate attendee rows. Verifiable directly from the diff.

judged_text: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refine its client-side twin enforces, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes emails already on the booking, never duplicates within the request, so createMany inserts one row per array entry. A direct addGuests mutation with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] — the dialog's refine being client-only — writes two attendee rows for the same person on one booking, producing duplicate confirmation emails and duplicate ICS attendee entries, and two concurrent requests adding the same email race past the read-filter-write sequence identically.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: client-only uniqueness check exists in `AddGuestsDialog` via `z.array(...).refine(...)`, but server `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` is only `z.array(z.string().email())` (no uniqueness). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones, but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array; `createMany` then inserts one attendee per entry, so `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` can create duplicate attendee rows/emails/ICS entries. The noted race condition is also plausible given the read-filter-write sequence and no shown DB uniqueness constraint.
